shlokas.translation: Just as an arrow loosed by Rāghava flies with the speed of the wind, so I shall go to Laṅkā, the city Rāvaṇa guards.
shlokas.context: On Mount Mahendra, Hanumān gathers himself for the leap across the ocean and tells the vānaras how he will go.
shlokas.speaker: Hanumān (to the vānaras)
teaches: optative gacchet ("would go") and future gamiṣyāmi
final t → d before a voiced sound
compounds with a past participle: rāvaṇa-pālitā "guarded by Rāvaṇa"

shlokas.translation: The time for my task presses, and the day is passing. I have given my promise: I must not stop here on the way.
shlokas.context: Halfway across the ocean, the mountain Maināka rises from the water and offers Hanumān a rest. Hanumān thanks him and declines.
shlokas.speaker: Hanumān (to Maināka)
teaches: instrumental of the agent: mayā dattā "given by me"
gerundive of duty: na sthātavyam "one must not stop"
hiatus at the pāda break (me | ahaḥ)

shlokas.translation: He saw her, thin from fasting and full of sorrow, sighing again and again, spotless like the thin first streak of the moon at the start of the bright fortnight.
shlokas.context: In the Aśoka grove Hanumān, hidden in a tree, sees Sītā for the first time: in a soiled garment, guarded by rākṣasīs (the line before), and pale with grief.
shlokas.speaker: Vālmīki (narrator)
teaches: accusatives agreeing with an object left unsaid ("her")

shlokas.translation: Placing a blade of grass between them, she of the pure smile replied: "Turn your mind away from me. Let your mind rest on your own people."
shlokas.context: Rāvaṇa comes to the Aśoka grove and tries to win Sītā with threats and promises. She will not even speak to him directly: she puts a blade of grass between them and answers.
shlokas.speaker: Sītā (to Rāvaṇa)
teaches: passive imperative kriyatām "let it be done"

shlokas.translation: "Noble lady, I am a vānara, the messenger of wise Rāma. Look, my queen: this ring is marked with Rāma's name."
shlokas.context: Hanumān has climbed down from the tree. Sītā is afraid he is Rāvaṇa in disguise, so he gives her proof: Rāma's own signet ring.
shlokas.speaker: Hanumān (to Sītā)

shlokas.translation: Blessed are they, the best of men, the great-souled ones who hold back rising anger with good sense, as one puts out a blazing fire with water.
shlokas.context: Hanumān has set Laṅkā on fire. When the flames die down he is struck with fear: did the fire reach Sītā too? He blames his own anger.
shlokas.speaker: Hanumān (to himself)

shlokas.translation: "Rāma, Kausalyā is blessed in her son! Take heart, you who keep your vows. The queen has been found, there is no doubt, and by none other than Hanumān."
shlokas.context: Dadhimukha runs to Sugrīva: the returning vānaras have stormed his honey grove. Sugrīva understands at once that they would never dare unless the search had succeeded, and he tells Rāma the good news.
shlokas.speaker: Sugrīva (to Rāma)
teaches: the same first pāda as the dawn verse कौसल्या सुप्रजा राम (1.23.2)
past participle as the verb: dṛṣṭā devī "the queen (has been) seen"

shlokas.translation: "If Rāma's beloved wife is not given back of your own accord, the city of Laṅkā will surely perish, and all its brave rākṣasas with it."
shlokas.context: In Rāvaṇa's council the generals boast that they will crush Rāma. Vibhīṣaṇa, Rāvaṇa's younger brother, alone speaks against them and begs him to return Sītā.
shlokas.speaker: Vibhīṣaṇa (to Rāvaṇa)

shlokas.translation: Then from the middle of the sea the Ocean himself rose up, like the sun rising from Meru, the great mountain.
shlokas.context: For three days Rāma has asked the Ocean for a way across, and the Ocean has not answered. Rāma draws his bow in anger, and the Ocean-lord rises from the deep to meet him.
shlokas.speaker: Vālmīki (narrator)
teaches: past participle as the verb: utthitaḥ "rose"

shlokas.translation: Though they beat him, the huge-bodied rākṣasa did not wake, and a thousand elephants were driven across his body.
shlokas.context: Rāvaṇa has sent his servants to wake his giant brother Kumbhakarṇa, who sleeps for months at a time. They blow conches, beat drums and pound him with clubs, and still he sleeps.
shlokas.speaker: Vālmīki (narrator)
teaches: genitive "of": vāraṇānām sahasram "a thousand of elephants"

shlokas.translation: (Bring) the herb that brings the dead back to life, and the one that draws out arrows, the one that restores the body's golden glow, and the great herb that joins wounds together.
shlokas.context: Indrajit's weapon has struck down Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa and most of the army. The old bear Jāmbavān sends Hanumān to a mountain of herbs in the Himālaya and names the four herbs he must bring.
shlokas.speaker: Jāmbavān (to Hanumān)
teaches: four accusative objects (the verb, "bring", is in the next verse)
the agent suffix -karaṇī "the one that makes"

shlokas.translation: "If Rāma, son of Daśaratha, is righteous and true to his word, and has no rival in valour, then, arrow, slay this son of Rāvaṇa!"
shlokas.context: Lakṣmaṇa has fought Indrajit, Rāvaṇa's son, for three days. He fits a last arrow to his bow and makes an act of truth: if Rāma is truly righteous, let the arrow kill Indrajit. It does.
shlokas.speaker: Lakṣmaṇa (to his arrow)
teaches: patronymics: dāśarathi "son of Daśaratha", rāvaṇi "son of Rāvaṇa"

shlokas.translation: "Here is the bridge I had built across the ocean, the great sea of waters, for your sake, wide-eyed one: Nala's bridge, so hard to make."
shlokas.context: Flying home in the Puṣpaka chariot after the war, Rāma shows Sītā the places of their story from the sky. Below them, the bridge still crosses the sea.
shlokas.speaker: Rāma (to Sītā)
teaches: passive with the instrumental: mayā baddhaḥ "built by me"

shlokas.translation: "King, here is your kingdom, kept safe; I hand it back to you. Today my life has reached its goal, and my heart's wish has come true."
shlokas.context: Rāma is home. Bharata, who ruled for fourteen years in Rāma's name with Rāma's sandals on the throne, puts the sandals back on his brother's feet and returns the kingdom.
shlokas.speaker: Bharata (to Rāma)
teaches: past participles in a passive sentence: rājyaṃ niryātitaṃ mayā "the kingdom (is) handed back by me"

shlokas.translation: While Rāma ruled the kingdom, no widows mourned, no one feared wild beasts, and no one feared sickness.
shlokas.context: The last sarga of the Yuddha-kāṇḍa: Rāma is crowned in Ayodhyā, and the poet describes his reign, Rāma-rājya.
